Sanskrit_Shloka: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥
English_Meaning: You have the right to perform your duty, but not to control the results. Do not work only for rewards, and do not become attached to inaction.
Interpretation: Success comes from sincere effort rather than constant worry about outcomes
Practical_Solution: Follow a study plan and focus on daily progress

Sanskrit_Shloka: योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय । सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते ॥
English_Meaning: Perform your actions with a balanced mind, giving up attachment. Be steady in success and failure; this balance is called Yoga.
Teaching: Maintain balance in success and failure
Interpretation: Failure is an opportunity to learn and improve
Practical_Solution: Accept outcomes calmly and continue working

Sanskrit_Shloka: क्रोधाद्भवति सम्मोहः सम्मोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः । स्मृतिभ्रंशाद् बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति ॥
English_Meaning: From anger comes delusion; from delusion comes confusion of memory; from confused memory wisdom is lost, and when wisdom is lost, one falls.
Interpretation: Uncontrolled anger leads to poor decisions
Practical_Solution: Pause before reacting and practice self-control

Sanskrit_Shloka: नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः । शरीरयात्रापि च ते न प्रसिद्ध्येदकर्मणः ॥
English_Meaning: Perform your prescribed duty, because action is better than inaction. Even the maintenance of the body is not possible without action.
Practical_Solution: Start with small tasks and maintain consistency

Sanskrit_Shloka: इति ते ज्ञानमाख्यातं गुह्याद्गुह्यतरं मया । विमृश्यैतदशेषेण यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु ॥
English_Meaning: I have explained this deep wisdom to you. Reflect on it fully, and then act according to your understanding.
Interpretation: Clear thinking leads to better choices
Practical_Solution: List options and evaluate them carefully

Sanskrit_Shloka: मात्रास्पर्शास्तु कौन्तेय शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः । आगमापायिनोऽनित्यास्तांस्तितिक्षस्व भारत ॥
English_Meaning: Pleasure and pain arise from contact with the senses; they come and go and are temporary. Endure them with patience.
Interpretation: Difficult situations do not last forever
Practical_Solution: Stay patient and continue positive efforts

Sanskrit_Shloka: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः ॥
English_Meaning: It is better to follow one’s own duty, even imperfectly, than to follow another’s duty perfectly. One’s own path is safer and more meaningful.
Practical_Solution: Focus on personal growth rather than comparison

Sanskrit_Shloka: उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥
English_Meaning: Lift yourself by your own mind and do not degrade yourself. The mind can be your friend, and the mind can also become your enemy.
Interpretation: The mind can be your friend or enemy
Practical_Solution: Focus on present actions

Sanskrit_Shloka: श्रद्धावाँल्लभते ज्ञानं तत्परः संयतेन्द्रियः । ज्ञानं लब्ध्वा परां शान्तिमचिरेणाधिगच्छति ॥
English_Meaning: A faithful and disciplined person gains knowledge. After gaining knowledge, one quickly attains deep peace.
Practical_Solution: Recognize your strengths and keep learning

Sanskrit_Shloka: यतो यतो निश्चरति मनश्चञ्चलमस्थिरम् । ततस्ततो नियम्यैतदात्मन्येव वशं नयेत् ॥
English_Meaning: Whenever the restless mind wanders away, bring it back gently and place it under the control of the Self.
Practical_Solution: Create and follow a daily routine

Sanskrit_Shloka: तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर । असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः ॥
English_Meaning: Therefore, perform your duty regularly without attachment. By working without attachment, a person reaches the highest state.
Practical_Solution: Set achievable goals and stay committed

Sanskrit_Shloka: यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः । स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्तते ॥
English_Meaning: Whatever a great person does, others follow. The example set by a leader becomes a standard for society.
Interpretation: People follow actions more than words
Practical_Solution: Demonstrate desired behavior

Sanskrit_Shloka: सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज । अहं त्वां सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः ॥
English_Meaning: Let go of fear and surrender to the Divine with trust. I will free you from all difficulties; do not grieve.
Teaching: Surrender fear and act with wisdom
Interpretation: Trust righteous decisions after careful thought
Practical_Solution: Choose based on values and responsibility

Sanskrit_Shloka: अद्वेष्टा सर्वभूतानां मैत्रः करुण एव च । निर्ममो निरहङ्कारः समदुःखसुखः क्षमी ॥
English_Meaning: One who has no hatred toward any being, who is friendly, compassionate, free from ego, balanced in joy and sorrow, and forgiving, is dear to the Divine.
Practical_Solution: Listen patiently and communicate respectfully

Sanskrit_Shloka: सुखदुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ । ततो युद्धाय युज्यस्व नैवं पापमवाप्स्यसि ॥
English_Meaning: Treat pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat with balance. Act with such steadiness and you will not be disturbed.
Practical_Solution: Focus on long-term goals

Sanskrit_Shloka: बुद्धियुक्तो जहातीह उभे सुकृतदुष्कृते । तस्माद्योगाय युज्यस्व योगः कर्मसु कौशलम् ॥
English_Meaning: A person with balanced wisdom rises above both good and bad results. Therefore, practice Yoga; Yoga is skill in action.
Practical_Solution: Analyze mistakes and try again

Sanskrit_Shloka: अभयं सत्त्वसंशुद्धिर्ज्ञानयोगव्यवस्थितिः । दानं दमश्च यज्ञश्च स्वाध्यायस्तप आर्जवम् ॥
English_Meaning: Fearlessness, purity of mind, steadiness in knowledge, charity, self-control, sacrifice, study, discipline, and honesty are divine qualities.
Practical_Solution: Remain grounded and continue learning

Sanskrit_Shloka: अज्ञश्चाश्रद्दधानश्च संशयात्मा विनश्यति । नायं लोकोऽस्ति न परो न सुखं संशयात्मनः ॥
English_Meaning: The ignorant, faithless, and doubting person loses direction. One filled with constant doubt finds neither peace nor happiness.
Practical_Solution: Take one step at a time with confidence

Sanskrit_Shloka: असंशयं महाबाहो मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलम् । अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते ॥
English_Meaning: The mind is restless and difficult to control, but through practice and detachment it can be disciplined.
Teaching: Practice and detachment control the mind
Interpretation: Habits change through repetition and discipline
Practical_Solution: Replace bad habits with positive routines

Sanskrit_Shloka: यतः प्रवृत्तिर्भूतानां येन सर्वमिदं ततम् । स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य सिद्धिं विन्दति मानवः ॥
English_Meaning: By performing one’s own work as an offering to the Divine source of all beings, a person attains fulfillment.
Practical_Solution: Identify your strengths and use them positively
